cards.question:
Unstable partition (predicate)

Rearrange an array so that elements satisfying a predicate come before items not satisfying the predicate.

Count elements satisfying predicate

How many elements satisfy the predicate at the completion of the the classic two-region partitioning algorithm?

Unstable partition array around a pivot

Rearrange an array so that elements less than the pivot come before elements greater than or equal to it.

Unstable partition using two indices

Rearrange an array so that elements satisfying a predicate come before items not satisfying the predicate.
Use separate `l` and `r` indices.

Stable partition with auxiliary array

Rearrange an array so that all elements satisfying a predicate come before all elements that do not, while preserving relative order within both groups.
Use an auxiliary array.

Hoare partition

Rearrange the elements in the array segment `[lo, hi]` around a pivot taken from the segment and return an index `split` so that, on termination, every element in `[lo, split]` is `<= pivot` and every element in `[split + 1, hi]` is `>= pivot`.

Three-way partition invariants

State the invariants in the three-way partition problem:

- after each loop iteration
- upon termination
cards.answer:
After each iteration:

- `[0, lt)`: known < pivot
- `[lt, i)`: known == pivot
- `[i, gt]`: unknown
- `[gt + 1, n)` known > pivot

At termination `i == gt + 1` and:

- `[0, lt)`: known < pivot
- `[lt, gt]`: known == pivot
- `[gt + 1, n)`: known > pivot
